assessment.nobel_worthiness: An extraordinarily ambitious fiction that enlarges the novel's range through verbal invention, historical imagination, comic force and searching accounts of systems of power.
assessment.attribution: For an encyclopedic fiction that has transformed the possibilities of narrative, historical inquiry and linguistic play.
assessment.maturity: The achievement is sustained across major novels of strikingly different scale and design, with Gravity’s Rainbow and Mason & Dixon central to a durable body of work.
uncertainties: Assessment necessarily rests on incomplete coverage of a technically dense and extensive oeuvre.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A major renewal of modern Arabic poetry whose mythic, fractured and intellectually adventurous lyric language has created an enduring poetic world.
assessment.attribution: For renewing Arabic lyric poetry through a sustained dialogue between inherited forms, modernity and exile.
assessment.maturity: The long poetic and essayistic career gives the contribution exceptional historical depth and formal continuity.
uncertainties: Translation cannot fully convey prosodic, linguistic and intertextual achievement in Arabic.
Corpus coverage of the extensive poetry and essays is necessarily partial.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Carson's singular hybrid practice remakes relations among classical learning, lyric compression, narrative, translation and visual form with unusual intellectual and emotional force.
assessment.attribution: For a radically inventive body of writing that makes classical knowledge newly active in contemporary lyric and narrative forms.
assessment.maturity: Works including Autobiography of Red and Nox demonstrate a sustained capacity for formal risk rather than a single method.
uncertainties: The relative weight of her work across poetry, scholarship, translation and performance forms requires careful whole-corpus consideration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A visionary prose project of remarkable imaginative amplitude, in which memory, bodily experience and urban and historical reality become densely patterned metaphysical fiction.
assessment.attribution: For a visionary fiction that has expanded the novel's powers of memory, dream and metaphysical inquiry.
assessment.maturity: The achievement appears sustained across fiction and poetry, with Blinding and Solenoid representing an ambitious mature architecture.
uncertainties: The assessment depends substantially on translations from Romanian and on incomplete access to the full corpus.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Tawada makes bilingual estrangement into a generative literary principle, producing original work on language, migration, species and imagination across several forms.
assessment.attribution: For a bilingual oeuvre that turns linguistic displacement into new fictional, poetic and dramatic possibilities.
assessment.maturity: Her work in Japanese and German displays sustained formal curiosity and range, rather than a limited bilingual experiment.
uncertainties: No single translation can settle the relation between the Japanese- and German-language bodies of work.
Assessment of multilingual wordplay is limited without full original-language coverage.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Yan Lianke's grotesque, allegorical and often disquieting fiction gives ideological violence and social transformation a distinctive imaginative form rather than merely documentary treatment.
assessment.attribution: For a fiercely inventive fiction exposing the human consequences of ideology, development and historical amnesia.
assessment.maturity: The representative novels suggest a substantial, evolving oeuvre with a recognizable moral and formal pressure.
uncertainties: Translation from Chinese may flatten tonal, stylistic and cultural registers.
The full relation of the novels to the essayistic work needs broader corpus assessment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Wright's large, polyphonic novels bring Indigenous sovereignty, oral forms and ecological time into an original and demanding reimagining of narrative scale.
assessment.attribution: For a powerful fiction that renews the novel through Indigenous knowledge, polyphony and ecological imagination.
assessment.maturity: Carpentaria and The Swan Book indicate an ambitious body of work whose formal commitments have been sustained across major novels.
uncertainties: The assessment should be tested against fuller coverage of the nonfiction and the complete fictional corpus.
The literary force of oral and cultural registers may not be fully captured by general critical description.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ulitskaya's interwoven narratives join moral seriousness with plural perspectives on Soviet and post-Soviet history, dissent and spiritual life.
assessment.attribution: For a humane and polyphonic fiction illuminating private conscience and historical experience in Russia.
assessment.maturity: The representative novels point to a substantial sustained oeuvre able to connect intimate lives with broad historical questions.
uncertainties: Translation from Russian may not fully transmit tonal nuance and stylistic texture.
A fuller appraisal would require broader coverage beyond the best-known novels.
